html:
A Pakistani theoretical physicist who shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg for the theory that unites the weak nuclear force and electromagnetism. He lived from 1926 to 1996.

Born in Jhang in the Punjab, he was a brilliant student and went to Cambridge, where he did his doctorate. He became a professor at Imperial College London. The electroweak theory he helped build predicted new particles, the W and Z bosons, found at CERN in 1983, and it is a pillar of the Standard Model of particle physics.

He worked hard for science in poor countries. In 1964 he founded the International Centre for Theoretical Physics in Trieste, Italy, where physicists from the developing world could do research. He also advised Pakistan's government and helped set up its space and atomic energy agencies.

He was a devout member of the Ahmadiyya community. After Pakistan declared Ahmadis non-Muslim in 1974, he largely left in protest. He was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate, but his home country long played down his fame. His gravestone called him the first Muslim Nobel laureate; officials later erased the word "Muslim".
sum: A Pakistani theoretical physicist who shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg for the theory that unites the weak nuclear force and electromagnetism. He lived from 1926 to 1996.
